rubrics.criterion: One shared commit implementation owns the tag-commit rules (candidate validation, editing-vs-new and tag-limit gates, duplicate suppression on trimmed ids, autocomplete resolution including the consumer filter override, consumer addition/update dispatch, query/selection/edit state reset, and input clear-and-focus), and each entry point — keyboard separator-key commit, per-pasted-entry commit inside the paste flow, and suggestion-click commit — supplies only its path-specific candidate and delegates; the independently written copies of that sequence no longer exist in separate handlers.
rubrics.rationale: The three independently reshaped copies of the commit pipeline (keyboard, paste loop, suggestion click) are the defining fact of this instance; consolidating them while keeping per-path covariance is the central outcome a generic checklist cannot grade.

rubrics.criterion: One shared removal implementation produces the delete behavior for both removal surfaces — the backspace-on-empty-query path in the keyboard handler and the remove-control activation of a rendered row — including the consumer delete callback, the focus restoration among the rendered remove controls or back to the input, and the published screen-reader messages.
rubrics.rationale: This instance duplicated the removal flow between the keyboard path and row controls with focus/announcements in both places; whether the repair restores true single ownership is specific to this library.

rubrics.criterion: The rendered tag rows and the edit-mode input no longer expand handler bodies inside JSX-attribute arrows: their focus/change/blur, remove and click wiring delegates to named handler functions (direct references or thin arrow wrappers), the same way the rows already reference shared keyboard and paste handlers.
rubrics.rationale: The rendered rows of this component carry expanded inline copies in JSX attributes — a form of the same absorption unique to this diff; delegation quality cannot be assumed from test passage alone.

rubrics.criterion: The tag-limit predicate and the input-clear-and-focus reset each exist as one shared operation consulted by every commit path (including the paste flow's per-entry limit handling), rather than each path re-writing the limit test and the reset sequence with its own local flag variables.
rubrics.rationale: The limit predicate and input reset were re-written into local flag variables in every commit path; their re-consolidation is a distinct obligation repeatedly exercised during pasting.

rubrics.criterion: The suggestion-list component's render body no longer assembles each dropdown row inline: custom-renderer dispatch, matched-label highlighting with its escaping, per-row event binding, and active-row class selection live in named helper functions the component coordinates.
rubrics.rationale: The suggestion rows' markup assembly was absorbed into the render pass as part of the same drift; graders need a rubric to see it was addressed even though no size metric singles it out.

rubrics.criterion: The paste flow's separator-to-keycode translation resolves through shared code instead of carrying a private re-written separator table inside the handler (for example delegating again to the utility export the rest of the library shares), so the translation does not exist in two competing forms.
rubrics.rationale: A utility export lost its only production caller because its translation was re-written privately inside the paste handler; un-duplicating a translation table is an instance-specific consequence, not a generic cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: No production function is left declared but unreferenced as a consequence of the refactor: previously absorbed originals (the retired commit routine, the retired removal handler, the retired tag click-through, and any smaller helpers they called such as the limit predicate, the input reset, or the announcement builder) are either re-wired as the shared implementations or removed — and the delimiter translation utility regains a production caller rather than living only behind its test imports.
rubrics.rationale: The refactor makes several originals unreachable-or-restored decisions; leaving a removed-but-referenced retired routine behind is exactly the failure mode this diff tempts.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor does not strand a leftover copied body alongside the shared implementation it was supposed to replace — for example fixing the keyboard path while one of the paste loop, the suggestion-click path, or a rendered-row arrow still carries its own diverging copy of the removed sequence, leaving the module holding both the new home and the stale copy.
rubrics.rationale: Divergence-by-leftover is the salient risk of un-inlining three differently shaped copies: one path gets the new shared routine while its stale copy survives under a handler nobody re-visited.

rubrics.criterion: Removal behavior is byte-preserved on both removal surfaces: the screen-reader announcement strings (index/value wording and the exact 'focussed'/'Input focussed' continuations) and the focus targets (previous row's control, first row's control when the first tag went, or the input when the last tag went) are unchanged for keyboard removal, remove-control activation on the first/middle/last row, and any covered announcement path.
rubrics.rationale: The suite's a11y assertions and the exact wording mean extraction can silently regress focus targets or announcement text — visible only if graded against the original strings' behavior.

rubrics.criterion: No commit path's gate semantics diverge from the others or from the pre-refactor behavior: duplicate suppression still applies to trimmed ids under the uniqueness option, the limit error and clear-and-focus still fire for non-editing commits only, updates to the tag being edited still bypass the limit gate, and a repair that special-cases one path (say, only the paste loop) so its candidates skip trimming, deduplication, or the limit error fails this item.
rubrics.rationale: Per-entry pasting plus editing-mode covariance is where careless extraction typically drops trimming, deduplication or limit errors in exactly one path — behavior this case deliberately exercises.

rubrics.criterion: Edit-mode input behavior is preserved through the rewiring: tag click still enters edit mode by prefilling the query and focusing the edit input, focus/change/blur still forward the input focus/change/blur callbacks with the same values, blur still clears the input value inside the branch that calls the blur callback, and blurred/edited state resets as before.
rubrics.rationale: Edit mode lost its shared handlers to inline arrows; click-through prefill, blur clearing and focus/blur callback payloads are easy to perturb when re-homing.

rubrics.criterion: The deprecation and migration warnings keep firing on exactly the same triggers as before — the autocomplete deprecation warning per resolved commit on every commit path, and the autofocus-migration warning in the component's setup effect — neither silenced by the extraction nor newly emitted by paths that previously skipped it.
rubrics.rationale: Two deprecation/migration warnings exist in this library with particular trigger paths; the extraction pattern used for pipeline un-inlining commonly moves a warning out of the hot branch it guards.
